name: NPER
description: NPER returns the total number of payment periods required to reach a target value given a fixed interest rate and payment.
tldr: Calculates the number of periods for a loan or investment.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: 0 = end of period (default), 1 = beginning of period.

basicExample.description: Number of payments to pay off a loan
basicExample.explanation: Paying $500 per month on a $10,000 loan at 6% annual interest takes about 22.43 months.

advancedExamples.title: Reach a savings goal
advancedExamples.description: How many months to reach $10,000 by saving $300 per month at 5%?
advancedExamples.explanation: It takes about 32 months to reach the goal.

howItWorks: NPER solves for the number of periods in the time-value-of-money equation. It is the inverse of PMT.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Returns a decimal; round up if you need a whole number of periods.

commonErrors.cause: The payment is too small to reach the future value at the given rate.
commonErrors.fix: Increase the payment, lower the rate, or reduce the target amount.

commonErrors.cause: Result is not a whole number.
commonErrors.fix: Use ROUNDUP or CEILING to get the next whole period.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: NPER works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between NPER and PMT?
faq.answer: NPER solves for the number of payments. PMT solves for the payment amount.

faq.question: Can NPER handle zero interest?
faq.answer: Yes, NPER divides the target by the payment when rate is zero.

faq.question: Why is NPER negative?
faq.answer: The sign depends on the cash-flow convention. Use ABS to display a positive number.
